caption: How a cross-site request forgery works, and how the SameSite cookie attribute helps against it.

hook.text: Another site can act as you

problem.narration: In a cross-site request forgery attack, an attacker tricks your browser into making a request to a site you are logged in to. Imagine a random page quietly asking your bank to move money. The request includes your credentials, so the server carries out some harmful action, thinking that you intended it.

fix.narration: The fix lives in the cookie. The SameSite attribute controls when a browser is allowed to include the cookie in a cross-site request. With the Strict value, the browser will not include the cookie in any cross-site request. It provides some protection against CSRF attacks, though not a complete answer.

summary.narration: Three steps. Another site sends a request. The browser attaches the cookie. And SameSite cuts the cookie off.

outro.narration: If SameSite finally clicked, there are many more breakdowns on elvaric.
